name: Premature Closure of the Arterial Duct
aliases: Early closure of the ductus arteriosus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal and neonatal echocardiographic criteria for premature ductal closure

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of ductus arteriosus closure before birth or within the first days of life
Signs of pulmonary hypertension on echocardiography or clinical examination
Right ventricular hypertrophy detected by imaging or ECG
Presence of fetal hydrops or heart failure signs in utero

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic evidence of premature ductal closure plus at least one major clinical or imaging sign such as pulmonary hypertension or right ventricular hypertrophy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on prenatal or early neonatal echocardiography combined with clinical findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prenatal echocardiographic absence of ductal flow
searchTerms: no blood flow in ductus arteriosus before birth
prenatal heart ultrasound shows absent ductal flow
high blood pressure in newborn lungs
increased lung artery pressure in infant
cyanosis due to poor oxygen levels
swelling and fatigue from right heart failure
puffy hands or feet in baby

occasional.symptomName: Hepatomegaly secondary to right heart strain
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart strain
liver swelling due to heart problems
brain damage due to low oxygen

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating cardiac strain
imaging: Prenatal and neonatal echocardiography demonstrating absent or prematurely closed ductus arteriosus
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular congestion
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; may be associated with maternal NSAID exposure
other: Maternal history of NSAID use or indomethacin during pregnancy
Signs of fetal distress on prenatal monitoring

distinguishingFeatures: Echocardiographic evidence of patent ductus arteriosus with left-to-right shunting
Absence of pulmonary hypertension in early neonatal period
Normal ductus arteriosus flow on echocardiography
May have associated lung parenchymal abnormalities

redFlags: Severe neonatal hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Signs of right heart failure in the neonate
Fetal hydrops detected on prenatal ultrasound
references: Rychik J, et al. Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus: diagnosis and management. Pediatric Cardiology. 2018.
McNamara PJ, et al. Neonatal pulmonary hypertension: pathophysiology and treatment. Clinics in Perinatology. 2020.
Orphanet: Premature closure of the arterial duct (ORPHA:95486)
